final.answer: The item directly upstream of CHV-2-2 in the process flow is FV-2-2, and its datasheet is indeed for the Fisher ET. final.answer: The transmitter FT-2-2 (Rosemount 3051) has no fixed fail state: on a sensor or microprocessor failure the 4-20 mA output is driven either high or low, and which one occurs is selected by an internal jumper/switch setting in the device. Default alarm levels are high ≥ 21.75 mA and low ≤ 3.75 mA (NAMUR-compliant option: ≥ 22.5 mA / ≤ 3.6 mA; custom high 20.2–23.0 mA, low 3.6–3.8 mA). The datasheet does not state the step-by-step procedure or exact location for changing the jumper, so that part is not stated in the available documents.

final.answer: The documents don't identify which part is leaking or provide a diagnostic/checking procedure, so that part of the question is not stated. What the PV-2-1 datasheet (Fisher ET) does say: the valve's shutoff is achieved by the valve plug seal ring being forced (by a backup ring or spring-loading) against the cage, with seat rings as the seating parts. Shutoff is rated per ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4: Class IV is standard with metal seating, Class V/VI are optional (Class V requires spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring), and TSO trim is factory tested to no leakage at shipment (shutoff class V, water test medium). If the valve was ordered with TSO or Class V/VI trim, leakage when shut would indicate those sealing parts (plug seal ring and/or seat ring) are not performing to that rating, but the datasheet does not say how to determine which one is at fault.

Yes — the valve uses seat rings and a plug seal ring as its seating/shutoff parts, and its shutoff is rated by ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4 leakage classes: Class IV is standard with metal seating, Class V or VI are optional, and valves with TSO (Tight Shutoff) trim are factory tested to have no leakage at shipment (TSO is not an ANSI/FCI class) [p. 6].

Details from Table 4, "Shutoff Classifications Per ANSI/FCI 70-2 and IEC 60534-4" (see Table 4 on page 6; ANSI/FCI 70-2 and IEC 60534-4 are industry standards that define leakage classes — how much a closed valve may leak):

**Metal seating (all constructions except Cavitrol III cages):**
- Class IV — standard
- Class V — optional; requires spring-loaded seal ring, radius-seat plug and wide-bevel seat ring; not available with 8-in. port or quick-opening cage, and not with trims 4, 29 and 85
- Class VI — optional (see Table 6)

**PTFE seating (all constructions except Cavitrol III cages):**
- Class V Air Test and Class V — available
- Class VI — optional (see Table 6)

**Cavitrol III cages (ET only):**
- One-stage cage, metal seating: Class IV standard, Class V optional
- Two-stage cage, metal seating: Class V

**TSO trim (ET and EAT, CL125–600):** replaceable, protected soft seat; the TSO trim is factory tested to a more stringent Emerson requirement of no leakage at time of shipment, test medium is water (specify service P when ordering); shutoff class V. TSO is not an ANSI/FCI leakage class; for more information, contact your Emerson sales office [p. 6].

**On the seat ring / plug seal parts themselves:** the Features section (p. 3) describes the PTFE seating shutoff mechanism — a backup ring or spring-loading forces the valve plug seal ring against the cage (shown in Figure 3 on page 3). The General Application section (p. 2) notes metal-to-PTFE seating is standard in all valves except Cavitrol III cages (for stringent shutoff requirements), and metal-to-metal seating is optional for all other valves. The Trim Cartridge section (p. 6) lists seat leak test = CL V shutoff.

**Class VI conditions (Table 6 on page 7):** For the ET valve, Class VI is available with port sizes 3.4375 to 7 in. (not for use with NPS 8; limited retrofit capability — consult your Emerson sales office). Minimum seat load: 300 lbs/lineal inch for metal seat; for soft seat, see Catalog 14. Both soft seat and metal seat constructions can provide ANSI/FCI Class VI shutoff [p. 7].

I could not find in these facts any numeric leakage rate (e.g., bubbles per hour or drops per hour) for the classes themselves — the datasheet only names the classes and points to Table 6/Table 7 for Class VI capabilities.
